authentication_methods._comment: Fixed platform rules for Lab 33. The tenant's own settings (which methods are on for which groups, custom strengths, SSPR and TAP settings) live in the scenario data. Built-in strengths follow Microsoft Learn 'Authentication strengths' (2026); federated combinations and QR code are left out to keep the model small.

windowsHelloForBusiness.label: Windows Hello for Business / Platform Credential

sspr_method_map._comment: Registered authentication method -> SSPR method it counts as. SMS and voice share one mobile phone number, so they count once. Passkeys, Windows Hello, certificates and TAP are not SSPR methods. Hardware/software OATH are left out (support for SSPR varies; owner to check).

admin_sspr._comment: Administrator SSPR policy: always on for admin roles, always two methods, never security questions, whatever the tenant's user SSPR policy says.

concepts.authentication methods policy: The tenant setting that turns each sign-in method on or off and targets it at chosen groups, with exclusions winning over inclusions.
concepts.authentication strength: A Conditional Access grant control that lists exactly which method combinations may satisfy a sign-in.
concepts.phishing-resistant MFA: Methods bound to the real site by public-key cryptography, so a fake page cannot relay them: passkeys (FIDO2), Windows Hello for Business and multifactor certificate-based authentication.
concepts.number matching: Microsoft Authenticator push asks the user to type the number shown on the sign-in screen, which stops blind approval of MFA fatigue prompts.
concepts.Temporary Access Pass: A time-limited passcode an administrator issues so a user can sign in and register passwordless methods, optionally usable only once.
concepts.self-service password reset: Lets users reset their own password after proving who they are with the number of registered methods the policy requires.
concepts.custom authentication strength: An administrator-defined list of allowed combinations, for example passkeys restricted to approved key models by AAGUID.
